1	# RTK — Token-Optimized Commands
2	
3	## Golden Rule
4	
5	**Use `rtk` for any command whose output may exceed a few lines.** Inside WSL Remote sessions the global PreToolUse hook auto-rewrites Bash commands to their `rtk`-prefixed form (`git status` → `rtk git status`). On native Windows shells the hook is unavailable, so prefix explicitly. `rtk` passes through commands without a dedicated filter unchanged — always safe to use.
6	
7	```bash
8	# ✅ Correct (chains too)
9	rtk git add . && rtk git commit -m "msg" && rtk git push
10	```
11	
12	## Commands by Category
13	
14	```bash
15	# Git
16	rtk git status / log / diff / show / add / commit / push / pull / branch / fetch / stash
17	
18	# GitHub CLI
19	rtk gh pr list / view / create
20	rtk gh issue list / view
21	rtk gh run list
22	
23	# Build & Type Check
24	rtk tsc                  # TypeScript errors only, grouped by file
25	rtk lint                 # ESLint grouped by rule/file
26	rtk next build           # Next.js build compact
27	
28	# Tests
29	rtk test <cmd>           # generic — failures only
30	rtk vitest / jest / pytest / cargo test / go test
31	
32	# Files & Search
33	rtk ls <path>            # token-optimized tree
34	rtk read <file>          # smart file read
35	rtk grep <pattern> <path>
36	rtk find "*.ext" <path>
37	rtk diff <a> <b>
38	
39	# Containers
40	rtk docker ps / images / logs / compose ps / compose logs
41	rtk kubectl pods / logs / services
42	
43	# Data & Errors
44	rtk json <file>          # structure without values
45	rtk err <cmd>            # filter errors only from any command
46	rtk log <file>           # deduplicated log
47	rtk env -f <prefix>      # filtered env vars
48	rtk curl <url>           # truncate + save full output
49	
50	# Meta
51	rtk gain                 # token savings stats
52	rtk gain --history       # recent commands
53	rtk gain --daily         # day-by-day breakdown
54	rtk discover             # find missed savings opportunities
55	rtk init --show          # verify which AI tool integrations are active
56	```
57	
58	## When to Use
59	
60	Wrap any noisy command (`git`, `docker`, `tsc`, test runners, `find`, log files). Skip for commands that produce only a handful of lines. RTK passes through unknown commands transparently.
61	
62	## Setup Reference
63	
64	For installing RTK in a fresh project (Docker + WSL workflow), see `~/.claude/templates/rtk-setup.md`.

2	name: RTK token optimization — mandatory prefix
3	description: All Bash commands prefer `rtk` prefix; WSL Remote sessions auto-rewrite via PreToolUse hook, native Windows requires explicit prefix
4	type: feedback
5	originSessionId: f4145fdf-c8cb-416a-b0d7-4afed60e2439
6	---
7	Prefix Bash commands with `rtk` whenever output may exceed a few lines.
8	
9	**Why:** Noisy output (`git`, `tsc`, `docker`, test runners, file dumps) wastes the context window. RTK filters/compresses to 10–40% of the original size — 60–90% token savings on a typical 30-min session. Replaced CHOP entirely (2026-04-25) — chop is uninstalled, all rules now reference rtk.
10	
11	**How to apply:**
12	- WSL Remote (recommended): the global Claude Code PreToolUse hook (registered by `rtk init -g` inside WSL) auto-prefixes — no manual action needed.
13	- Native Windows shells (Git Bash, PowerShell): the hook does not run, so prefix explicitly. `rtk git status`, `rtk tsc --noEmit`, `rtk docker compose ps`, `rtk grep ...`.
14	- Short outputs (<5 lines, e.g. `git rev-parse HEAD`) may skip `rtk`.
15	- Project-level filters: `.rtk/filters.toml` overrides global behavior for `docker compose logs`, `php -l`, etc.
16	- Verify usage: `rtk gain` (zero counter ⇒ rtk not actually being invoked).
17	- **Do NOT use bash `cat`/`head`/`rtk read` to read files** — RTK has no `read` filter so it's 0% savings and wastes context. Always use Claude Code's built-in `Read` tool directly instead.
18
